summary: This wiki-derived infobox note summarizes key country facts about East Timor (Timor-Leste), a Southeast Asian state. It covers its official name and languages, capital Dili, government structure with President Francisco Guterres and Prime Minister Mari Alkatiri, and its history of independence declarations, Indonesian annexation, UN administration and restored independence. It also lists area, population, economic figures, HDI, currency and internet/calling codes.
one_line: Infobox-style overview of East Timor (Timor-Leste), covering its government, languages, history, population, economy and codes.
key_facts: East Timor's official name is Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste, with Tetum name Repúblika Demokrátika Timór Lorosa'e and Portuguese name República Democrática de Timor-Leste.
The capital and largest city of East Timor is Dili.
East Timor's official languages are Tetum and Portuguese.
The Constitution recognises fifteen further national languages besides Tetum and Portuguese.
96.9% of East Timor's population was Roman Catholic in 2010 according to the note.
East Timor is a unitary semi-presidential constitutional republic, with President Francisco Guterres and Prime Minister Mari Alkatiri.
East Timor declared independence on 28 November 1975.
Indonesia annexed East Timor on 17 July 1976.
East Timor was administered by UNTAET from 25 October 1999.
Independence was restored to East Timor on 20 May 2002.
East Timor's total area is 15,410 km (5,950 sq mi), ranked 154th.
The 2015 census recorded a population of 1,167,242 in East Timor.
East Timor's HDI was 0.605 in 2015, medium and ranked 133rd.
East Timor uses the United States Dollar (USD) as currency, and centavo coins are also used.
East Timor's calling code is +670 and its internet TLD is .tl, with time zone UTC+9 and driving on the left.
